Knowledge graphs

The context graphs you maintain. Build them, shape them, check they answer the use case — then the graph owner publishes with a sealed, attributable record.

Ask

A query engine, not a search box. Ask in plain language — a supervisor agent grounds the question in the knowledge graph, routes to source systems, and returns an evidence-backed answer with the full reasoning open for inspection.
Ask against …
Enter to ask · Esc to clear

Reports

A report here is a saved, governed, re-executable question — not a chart with numbers stored inside it. That is why the same report renders differently for each viewer, why every figure can name its source, and why a refresh changes the answer without changing the definition.

What report do you need?

Ask for it the way you would ask a colleague. I will read it back to you in one sentence first — nothing runs against your data until that sentence is right.

✦
Profiling is not a one-off. When a source changes shape — a new column, a distribution shift, a dictionary term that stops matching — the profiler raises a signal here rather than silently re-deriving the graph. Acting on a signal is a human decision because it can invalidate published answers.

Sources

Registered source systems and their connection health. Credentials are held by reference — Context Weave never stores a raw secret. Registering a source kicks off extraction and profiling automatically.

Trace & observability

Every answer carries a sealed, replayable trace. So does every report rendering — a view trace reconstructs what one viewer saw, under which predicate, at which as-of. Nothing here can be edited.

◈ sealed · immutable
Recent traces

Validation & evals

Continuous evaluation across eight dimensions for answers, plus publish-time spec validation for reports. Test scenarios are seeded from use-case hero questions.

Eval dimensions
Report-spec validation — run at publish, not at viewcomponent 06 gate · component 13 spec
Systematic failures—
Publish validation

✦
The regression gate is a publish precondition — a failing candidate cannot go live, and a report whose spec no longer resolves against the candidate graph blocks with it.

Feedback & learning

Every thumbs-down becomes a routed work item — on an answer or on a report figure. Nothing changes the system without validation and permission.

Inbox — routed by target
Learning pipeline
No feedback mutates the live system directly — every change flows through this pipeline and lands in a versioned release with a full audit record.

Audit & governance

Who did what, who can do what, what it costs, and what happens to data when sources leave.

Pending approvals—
Cost caps
80% triggers a soft warning; 100% hard-blocks with a governed override path. Caps are admin-editable; changes are audit events.

loading…
Choose a persona to sign in. Every screen after this one renders under the session it establishes. The persona decides which views exist; the scope decides which rows and which columns come back. They are two separate gates and this prototype never merges them — the second one is applied before the data reaches the browser, so what a persona cannot see is not on the page to be found.
Not a login form. There is no password here and there is no identity provider behind it. The thing being demonstrated is what happens after authentication — entitlement and data scope — so the prototype starts where a real deployment would hand off from SSO.

Credentials are held by reference only — Context Weave stores the vault pointer, never the secret itself. Rotation happens in your vault; nothing to update here.

Drop dictionary file
xlsx · csv · JSON — column descriptions, business terms, owners
The profiler compares its own semantic-class inference against your dictionary. Where they diverge by Δ>0.20 the column is flagged for review — the dictionary is evidence, not gospel.
✦
On finish: extraction runs, then profiling (job appears in Catalogue → Jobs). Disconnecting later is a soft-delete — data is retained and purge is governed in component 12.
